title: Met de trein
subtitle: Transport and separable verbs
intro: In this lesson you learn to buy a train ticket and talk about transport. You also learn how separable verbs work: **instappen** becomes **Ik stap in.**

grammar.title: Separable verbs: the prefix goes to the end
grammar.explanation: Many Dutch verbs have a prefix: **in**, **uit**, **over**, **aan**. In the present tense the prefix leaves the verb and goes to the end of the sentence. The verb part gets the normal present endings: **ik stap**, **jij stapt**, **wij stappen**.

rows: Ik kom om tien uur aan.

examples.nl: De trein komt om tien uur aan.
examples.en: The train arrives at ten o'clock.

grammar.tip: Ask: what is the prefix? Send it to the end: **in**, **uit**, **over**, **aan**.

grammar.title: The prefix usually comes at the very end
grammar.explanation: The prefix usually comes at the very end of the sentence, after the place and the time. In **Ik stap in Utrecht over**, the place **in Utrecht** comes before the prefix **over**. In a question the prefix also stays at the end: **Waar stap je over?**

rows: De trein komt om tien uur aan.
Hoe laat komt de trein aan?

examples.nl: Hoe laat komt de trein aan?
examples.en: What time does the train arrive?

grammar.tip: After the question word, the verb comes second, then the place, then the prefix at the end.

grammar.title: With a modal verb: keep the verb together
grammar.explanation: After **moeten**, **willen**, **kunnen** and **mogen**, the separable verb stays together as an infinitive at the end of the sentence. **Je moet in Utrecht overstappen.** Do not split it: not *Je moet in Utrecht over stappen.*

culture.title: Checking in and out
culture.text: In the Netherlands you check in at the start of your trip and check out at the end. You can use your ov-chipkaart or your bank card. If you forget to check out, you pay more. On the train, the conductor may ask for your ticket.

summary: Use **inchecken** at the start and **uitchecken** at the end of your trip.
Separable verbs split in the present: **Ik stap in.** **De trein komt aan.**
The prefix usually goes at the very end: **Ik stap in Utrecht over.**
With a modal verb the separable verb stays together at the end: **Je moet overstappen.**
